cves: MoguBlog through 6.2 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability that allows authenticated administrators to list other administrators' network-disk files via POST /networkDisk/getFileList. Attackers can query the endpoint, which filters only by status, file type, or filePath and never by admin_uid, to obtain other administrators' file names and download URLs.

MoguBlog through 6.2 contains a broken access control vulnerability that allows authenticated administrators to move or rename other administrators' network-disk files by supplying their file paths. Attackers can send crafted requests to POST /networkDisk/moveFile, batchMoveFile, or edit, which update rows without admin_uid checks, relocating or renaming other users' files and folders.

MoguBlog through 6.2 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability that allows authenticated administrators to delete other administrators' files via POST /networkDisk/deleteFile and batchDeleteFile. A vulnerability was detected in moxi624 Mogu Blog v2 up to 5.2. This affects the function BlogSortServiceImpl.addBlogSort of the file mogu_web/src/main/resources/templates/info.ftl of the component blogSort Endpoint. The manipulation of the argument sortName results in cross site scripting. The attack can be launched remotely. The project was informed of the problem early through an issue report...

MoguBlog through 6.2 exposes Elasticsearch index management endpoints in the mogu_search service without authentication, allowing remote attackers to delete, recreate, or alter the blog search index. Attackers can invoke POST endpoints to wipe the entire search index, delete specific documents, or inject malicious index entries, causing search functionality to return incorrect or no results.

MoguBlog through 6.2 fails to authenticate requests to the /web/comment/closeEmailNotification endpoint, allowing unauthenticated attackers to disable email notifications for arbitrary users. Remote callers can modify the startEmailNotification flag in Redis cache for any user identifier to suppress reply notifications without authorization.

MoguBlog through 6.2 fails to validate the comment author identity in the POST /web/comment/add endpoint, allowing authenticated users to post comments attributed to any other user. Attackers can supply arbitrary userUid values in the request body to impersonate other accounts including administrators.

MoguBlog through 6.2 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in the POST /pictureSort/getPictureSortByUid endpoint, which omits the @AuthorityVerify annotation required to enforce role-based permissions.
